explanations: putFile picks the shard by hashing ownerId:path, while getFile, listFolder and syncSince all route by ownerId alone. A file is therefore written to an essentially random shard per path, and reads, listings and sync only see the subset of files that happen to hash to the owner's shard. The partition key must be ownerId for writes too.

Partitioning by owner keeps all of one user's rows together, so a folder listing or sync is one prefix scan on one shard instead of a scatter-gather. It does not equalize file counts (large users create skew), does not enable cross-user sharing, and a folder rename still rewrites every row key under it.

All rows for one ownerId hash to the same shard, so a very large tenant concentrates load there. Nothing splits a single key across shards, ShardMap never rejects keys, and hash uniformity is over distinct keys, not over the volume behind one key.

A prefix scan returns every descendant, including deeper subfolders. Keeping only rows whose parent equals the folder yields direct children. The ownerId is already in the prefix, stored paths are already normalized, and there is no deletion marker in FileRecord.
